source_text: φύσις. Ἐν Χριστῷ δὴ οὖν ἡ πᾶσα καρποφορία καὶ πᾶσα προσαγωγή· φησὶ γὰρ αὐτὸς, «Χωρὶς ἐμοῦ, οὐ δύνασθε ποιεῖν οὐδέν.» Ὥσπερ γὰρ δι' αὐτοῦ τὴν προσαγωγὴν ἐσχήκαμεν, οὕτω καὶ πᾶσα θυσία δεκτὴ δι' αὐτοῦ, τῶν τὴν πίστιν εἰσδεδεγμένων. Ἐπαγγέλλεται δὲ τοῖς τὸ ἐκ γῆς ἱστᾶσι θυσιαστήριον, ἄφιξίν τε καὶ εὐλογίαν. «Ἥξω γὰρ,» φησὶ, «πρὸς σὲ, καὶ εὐλογήσω σε.» Παραδεξαμένοις γὰρ ἡμῖν διὰ τοῦ πανσόφου Μωσέως τῆς ἀληθείας τοὺς τύπους, καὶ αὕτη κατὰ καιροὺς ἐπέλαμψεν ἡ ἀλήθεια, τοῦτ' ἔστι Χριστὸς, δι' οὗ καὶ ἐν ᾧ τὴν ἄνωθεν εὐλογίαν καὶ παρὰ Πατρὸς πεπλουτήκαμεν, κατεσφραγισμένοι πρὸς υἱοθεσίαν ἐν ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, ἐν Χριστῷ δὲ δὴ πάλιν καὶ τοῦτο διαπεραίνεται. «Ἐὰν δὲ θυσιαστήριον ἐκ λίθων ποιῇς μοι,» φησὶν, «οὐκ οἰκοδομήσεις αὐτοὺς τμητούς.» Οὐκ ἐᾷ σιδήρῳ κατατιτρώσκεσθαι τοὺς ἀφιερωμένους τῷ Θεῷ λίθους. Λίθος γὰρ ἦν ἐκλεκτὸς, ἀκρογωνιαῖος, ἔντιμος, ὁ Χριστὸς, ἄτρωτος μὲν ἁμαρτίαις, τὰς δὲ ἐκ διαβόλου πληγὰς παθεῖν οὐκ εἰδὼς, οὐ μεμερισμένος Θεῷ τε καὶ κόσμῳ, καὶ εἰ γέγονε σὰρξ, ἀλλ' ὅλος ὢν ἅγιος, οὐ διαιρούμενος εἰς Θεὸν ἰδίᾳ, καὶ εἰς ἄνθρωπον ἰδικῶς μετὰ τὴν ἄῤῥητον ἕνωσιν, ἤτοι τὴν πρὸς σάρκα σύνοδον, ἀλλ' εἷς ὑπάρχων Θεὸς, καὶ ἄνθρωπος ὁ αὐτός. Μεμέρισται γὰρ οὐδαμῶς, καθὰ καὶ ὁ σοφὸς γράφει Παῦλος. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τὸ ἐκ γῆς οὖν ἄρα θυσιαστήριον, καὶ μὴν καὶ οἱ ἀπλῆγες λίθοι, σημαίνουσι Χριστὸν, κατὰ τοὺς ἤδη προειρημένους τρόπους; {ΚΥΡ.} Οὕτω φημί· πνευματικὸς γὰρ ὁ νόμος, κατὰ τὰς Γραφάς. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ τὸ Χριστοῦ μυστήριον, καὶ τὴν δι' αὐτοῦ πρόσοδον αἰνιγματωδῶς ὑπετύπου, τότε δὴ, τότε καὶ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας προαναδεῖξαι τὸ σχῆμα Θεὸς ἐσκέπτετο. Μωσέα μὲν οὖν ἐκάλει καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος τὸ Σινᾶ. Καὶ σύνες ἐντεῦθεν, ὅτι καὶ αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἁγίοις προφήταις δι' Υἱοῦ προσιτὸς ὁ Πατήρ· ἀναθρώσκουσι γὰρ ἀλλήλοις Μωσῆς τε καὶ Ἰησοῦς. Γέγραπται γὰρ, «Καὶ ἐλάλησε Κύριος πρὸς Μωσῆν λέγων· Εἶπον τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ λάβετέ μοι ἀπαρχὰς παρὰ πάντων, οἷς ἂν δόξῃ τῇ καρδίᾳ, λήψεσθε τὰς ἀπαρχάς μου, καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἀπαρχὴ, ἣν λήψεσθε παρ' αὐτῶν, χρυσίον καὶ ἀργύριον, χαλκὸν καὶ ὑακίνθινον, πορφύραν καὶ κόκκινον διπλοῦν, καὶ βυσσὸν κεκλωσμένην, καὶ τρίχας αἰγείας, καὶ δέρματα κριῶν ἠρυθροδανωμένα, καὶ δέρματα ὑακίνθινα, καὶ ξύλα ἄσηπτα, καὶ λίθους σαρδίου, καὶ λίθους εἰς τὴν γλυφὴν, εἰς τὴν ἐπωμίδα, καὶ εἰς τὸν ποδήρη, καὶ ποιήσεις μοι ἁγίασμα, καὶ ὀφθήσομαι ἐν ὑμῖν. Καὶ ποιήσεις μοι κατὰ πάντα ὅσα ἄν σοι δείξω ἐν τῷ ὄρει τὸ παράδειγμα τῆς σκηνῆς, καὶ τὸ παράδειγμα πάντων τῶν σκευῶν αὐτῆς, οὕτως ποιήσεις.» Ὁρᾷς ὅπως ἐπὶ τὸ χρῆναι καρποφορεῖν τὸ λυσιτελές τε καὶ χρειωδέστατον, εἰς Ἐκκλησίας σύστασιν προτρέπει λαοὺς, προσκομίζοντας ἱλαρῶς τὰ κατ' ἰσχύν τε καὶ γνώμην; Οὐ γάρ τοι χρυσὸν ἐζήτει μόνον
pass_a_gloss: [Nature (φύσις) — rendered in §3.] In Christ then all fruit-bearing (καρποφορία) and all offering/access (προσαγωγή); for he himself says, 'Without (χωρίς) me you can do nothing.' For as through him we have had (ἐσχήκαμεν) the access (προσαγωγή), so also every sacrifice acceptable (δεκτή) through him, of those who have received (εἰσδεδεγμένων) the faith. He promises (ἐπαγγέλλεται) to those setting up (ἱστᾶσι) the altar from earth arrival (ἄφιξις) and blessing (εὐλογία): 'For I will come to you and bless you.' For to us having received through the all-wise (πάνσοφος) Moses the types of the truth, also this truth shone forth (ἐπέλαμψεν) at the times (κατὰ καιρούς), that is Christ, through whom and in whom we have been enriched (πεπλουτήκαμεν) with the blessing from above and from the Father, sealed (κατεσφραγισμένοι) for adoption (υἱοθεσία) in the Holy Spirit; and in Christ again this too is accomplished (διαπεραίνεται). 'If you make me an altar of stones, you will not build them cut.' He does not allow the stones dedicated (ἀφιερωμένους) to God to be wounded (κατατιτρώσκεσθαι) by iron (σίδηρος). For Christ was a stone chosen (ἐκλεκτός), cornerstone (ἀκρογωνιαῖος), precious (ἔντιμος), unwounded (ἄτρωτος) by sins, not knowing to suffer the blows (πληγαί) from the devil, not divided (μεμερισμένος) between God and world, even if he became flesh, but being wholly holy, not divided (διαιρούμενος) into God privately and into man particularly after the ineffable (ἄρρητος) union (ἕνωσις), that is, the coming-together (σύνοδος) with flesh, but being one God and man the same. For he is in no way divided (μεμέρισται), as the wise Paul writes. PALL.: The altar from earth then, and the unstruck (ἀπλῆγες) stones, signify Christ, by the modes already said? CYR.: So I say; for the law is spiritual, according to the Scriptures. Since he was underfiguring (ὑπετύπου) enigmatically (αἰνιγματωδῶς) the mystery of Christ and the approach through him, then indeed then God considered (ἐσκέπτετο) to show beforehand (προαναδεῖξαι) the shape (σχῆμα) of the Church too. He called Moses and with him Jesus/Joshua (Ἰησοῦς) onto Mount Sinai. Understand from this that also to the holy prophets themselves the Father is accessible (προσιτός) through the Son; for Moses and Jesus leap up (ἀναθρώσκουσι) together. For it is written: 'The Lord spoke to Moses saying: Say to the sons of Israel, and take for me firstfruits (ἀπαρχαί) from all to whom it may seem in heart; you will take my firstfruits; and this is the firstfruit you will take from them: gold, silver, bronze, blue (ὑακίνθινον), purple (πορφύρα), double scarlet (κόκκινον διπλοῦν), spun fine linen (βύσσος κεκλωσμένη), goat hairs, rams' skins dyed red (ἠρυθροδανωμένα), blue skins, incorruptible woods (ξύλα ἄσηπτα), sardius stones, stones for carving (γλυφή), for the ephod (ἐπωμίς) and for the foot-length robe (ποδήρης); and you will make me a sanctuary (ἁγίασμα), and I will be seen (ὀφθήσομαι) among you. And you will make me according to all I show you on the mountain the pattern (παράδειγμα) of the tent and the pattern of all its vessels (σκεύη); so you will make.' You see how he urges (προτρέπει) peoples toward the need to bear as fruit the profitable and most useful (χρειωδέστατον) for the constitution (σύστασις) of the Church, bringing cheerfully (ἱλαρῶς) things according to strength (ἰσχύς) and will (γνώμη)? For he did not seek gold only
pass_b_english: Cyril: …In Christ, then, lies all our offering of fruit and every approach; for he himself says, ‘Apart from me you can do nothing’ (John 15:5). For just as through him we have obtained access (Romans 5:2), so too through him every sacrifice of those who have received the faith is acceptable. And to those who set up the altar of earth he promises his coming and a blessing: ‘For I will come to you,’ he says, ‘and bless you’ (Exodus 20:24). For when we had received through the all-wise Moses the types of the truth, the truth itself also shone forth in its due season, that is, Christ, through whom and in whom we have been enriched with the blessing that comes from above and from the Father (Ephesians 1:3), sealed for adoption as sons in the Holy Spirit (Ephesians 1:13). And this too, again, is fulfilled in Christ: ‘And if you make me an altar of stones,’ he says, ‘you shall not build them of hewn stones’ (Exodus 20:25). He does not allow the stones dedicated to God to be wounded with iron. For Christ was the chosen stone, the precious cornerstone (Isaiah 28:16; 1 Peter 2:6): unwounded by sins, and knowing nothing of suffering the blows that come from the devil; not divided between God and the world, even though he became flesh, but holy through and through; not divided into God separately and man separately after the ineffable union, that is, his coming together with flesh, but being one and the same, God and also man. For he is in no way divided, as the wise Paul also writes (1 Corinthians 1:13).
Palladius: So the altar of earth, and the uncut stones as well, signify Christ, in the ways already described?

Cyril: So I say; for the law is spiritual, as the Scriptures say (Romans 7:14). And once he had outlined in riddles the mystery of Christ and our approach through him, then, at that very point, God planned to show beforehand the form of the Church as well. So he called Moses, and Joshua with him, up onto Mount Sinai (Exodus 24:12–13). And understand from this that even to the holy prophets themselves the Father is approachable through the Son; for Moses and Joshua go up together. For it is written: ‘And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the sons of Israel, and take firstfruits for me from all whose heart moves them; you shall take my firstfruits. And these are the firstfruits that you shall take from them: gold and silver, bronze and blue, purple and double scarlet, and twisted fine linen, and goats’ hair, and rams’ skins dyed red, and skins dyed blue, and wood that does not decay, and sardius stones, and stones for engraving, for the ephod and for the robe that reaches to the feet. And you shall make me a sanctuary, and I will be seen among you. And you shall make it for me according to all that I show you on the mountain, the pattern of the tent and the pattern of all its furnishings; so you shall make it’ (Exodus 25:1–9). Do you see how he urges the peoples to bring as offering what is profitable and most needful for the building up of the Church, bringing gladly what matches their means and their will? For he did not ask only for gold…

choices.why: προσαγωγή carries both ‘offering’ and ‘access’; Cyril plays on both, so the first use is rendered ‘approach’ and the second ‘access’ (δι’ οὗ καὶ τὴν προσαγωγὴν ἐσχήκαμεν is the wording of Romans 5:2; Ephesians 2:18 is close).

Ἰησοῦς here is Joshua son of Nun, rendered ‘Joshua’ as in Books 2–8; Cyril's point that the Father is reached ‘through the Son’ rests on the fact that Joshua bears the name Jesus in Greek, which English cannot show without adding words.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

The row opens with φύσις, the last word of the sentence begun in section 3; it is rendered there. προσαγωγή carries both ‘offering’ and ‘access’; Cyril plays on both, so the first use is rendered ‘approach’ and the second ‘access’ (δι’ οὗ καὶ τὴν προσαγωγὴν ἐσχήκαμεν is the wording of Romans 5:2; Ephesians 2:18 is close). ‘Every sacrifice … acceptable through him’ may echo 1 Peter 2:5; left uncited. The pairing of Moses with types and Christ with truth recalls John 1:17, but Cyril does not quote it; left uncited. Ephesians 1:3 (blessing in Christ) and 1:13 (sealed with the Holy Spirit, with adoption from 1:5) are cited as clear allusions. Iron tools on altar stones echoes Deuteronomy 27:5; left uncited, since Cyril is explaining Exodus 20:25. Isaiah 28:16 LXX gives the adjectives in Cyril's order (ἐκλεκτὸν ἀκρογωνιαῖον ἔντιμον); 1 Peter 2:6 quotes it. 1 Corinthians 1:13 is Paul's question ‘Is Christ divided?’, which Cyril turns into a statement. Ἰησοῦς here is Joshua son of Nun, rendered ‘Joshua’ as in Books 2–8; Cyril's point that the Father is reached ‘through the Son’ rests on the fact that Joshua bears the name Jesus in Greek, which English cannot show without adding words. Exodus 24:12–13: God calls Moses up the mountain (24:12) and he goes up with Joshua (24:13). Exodus 25:1–9 follows the LXX (sardius stones, ‘I will be seen among you’, ξύλα ἄσηπτα, ‘wood that does not decay’, kept because Cyril later reads it of Christ's incorrupt body). The row ends mid-sentence; section 5 continues it.

changes: Isaiah 28:16 adjectives put in natural English order ('the chosen stone, the precious cornerstone')
ἰδίᾳ / ἰδικῶς: 'on his own' -> 'separately' (Christological term kept exact: no division after the union)
citation Exodus 24:13 -> Exodus 24:12–13 (the call up the mountain is 24:12; Joshua goes up in 24:13); bible_refs and note updated
Joshua kept as in Books 2–8; the Joshua = Jesus point is explained in the note, not added to the text
